    To beginBarry Allen prawn cocktailFrank tells Carl he's Barry Allen. Poached prawns, Marie Rose, iceberg, lemon.How to make it500g green king prawns, peeled, tails on1 lemon2 bay leaves125g whole-egg mayonnaise2 tbsp tomato sauce1 tsp Tabasco1/2 iceberg lettuce, finely shredded1 avocado, diced1 tsp sweet paprikaBring a pot of salted water to the boil with the bay leaves and half the lemon, add the prawns and poach until just pink, about 2 minutes.Plunge into iced water, then drain and chill.Mix the mayo, tomato sauce, Tabasco and a squeeze of lemon for the Marie Rose.Fill 4 coupes with lettuce and avocado, hang the prawns over the rim and spoon over the sauce.Dust with paprika and serve with lemon wedges.Strong family crab beignetsFrank says grace at the Strongs' table. Crab beignets, Creole remoulade, lemon.How to make it250g cooked crab meat, picked150g plain flour1 tsp baking powder1 egg150ml milk2 spring onions, sliced1 tsp Cajun seasoning125g whole-egg mayonnaise1 tbsp Creole or Dijon mustard1 tbsp capers, chopped1 lemon1 L vegetable oil, for fryingWhisk the flour, baking powder, egg and milk to a thick batter, then fold in the crab, spring onion and Cajun seasoning.Mix the mayo, mustard, capers and a squeeze of lemon for the remoulade.Fry spoonfuls in 180°C oil, turning, until puffed and golden, about 3 minutes.Drain, salt and serve hot with the remoulade and lemon.Hot hors d'oeuvres from the cartServed at cocktail hour, the way Maxim's did it for Pan Am.How to make itA house standard, not part of tonight's cook.Main courseFilet mignon from the aisle cartFrank flies as Pan Am pilot Frank Taylor. Filet, bearnaise, pommes dauphine, beans.How to make it4 beef eye fillet steaks, about 200g each2 tbsp olive oil150g butter, plus 30g for the steaks2 egg yolks2 tbsp white wine vinegar1 shallot, finely chopped2 tbsp tarragon, chopped500g floury potatoes, peeled60g plain flour2 eggs1 L vegetable oil, for frying200g green beansBoil and mash the potatoes dry. Heat 60ml water with 30g of the butter, beat in the flour, then the eggs, and mix into the mash.Fry spoonfuls of the potato in 180°C oil until puffed and golden for the pommes dauphine.Simmer the vinegar with the shallot and half the tarragon until almost gone, whisk in the yolks over low heat, then the 120g melted butter in a thin stream. Stir in the rest of the tarragon.Sear the seasoned steaks in the oil and remaining butter, about 4 minutes a side for medium-rare, and rest.Blanch the beans and plate everything the way the cart did it, sauce on the side.DessertBucket of cream pots de cremeTwo little mice fell in a bucket of cream. Vanilla custard pots, brown butter shortbread.How to make it500ml pouring cream1 vanilla bean, split5 egg yolks80g caster sugar125g butter, browned and cooled60g icing sugar175g plain flour1/2 tsp sea salt flakesHeat the cream with the vanilla until steaming. Whisk the yolks and caster sugar, then whisk in the hot cream.Strain into 4 small pots in a roasting tin, pour hot water halfway up and bake at 150°C until set with a wobble.Beat the browned butter with the icing sugar, mix in the flour and salt, press into a tin and bake at 160°C until golden.Chill the pots and serve with a wedge of the shortbread.From the trolleyPinstripe ManhattanNobody can stop staring at the pinstripes. Rye, sweet vermouth, bitters, cherry.How to make it240ml rye whiskey120ml sweet vermouth8 dashes of Angostura bitters4 maraschino cherries1 orange1 tray iceStir the rye, vermouth and bitters with plenty of ice until very cold.Strain into 4 chilled coupes.Add a cherry and twist a strip of orange peel over each.Heidsieck champagneTo the moon!How to make itA house standard, not part of tonight's cook.
